comparator.name: Dutch Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: Stage 2 checked 17 November 2026. Current BA-DST and 41 actual module bodies, programme OER effective 1 September 2026 and current faculty OER read. The former duplicate is resolved in the current catalogue; all 26 previous component IDs, names and weights are preserved, with the digital course placed in year two and a new distinct philosophy component added in year one: first-year Philosophy of Science 5000VPHSCY and second-year Humanities in a Digital World 5000VHDW2Y are distinct 5 EC courses. Preserve the corrected 120 EC first-two-year core, 10 EC academic reading/writing, 10 EC thesis and 30 EC genuine open study: 27 components and 170 documented EC. The concentration parent 15 EC versus 10 EC branches/two-module rule and exact full-cohort timetable/progression remain unverified. No arithmetic reconciliation or older-cohort replacement is assumed. No formal specialisations; Language/Culture are informal directions. Preserve skill-specific CEFR targets, ordered language/thesis entry, mandatory zero-credit seminar/symposium and elective approval, level and overlap conditions. Strongest cultural and empirical-language UCR responses were tested against actual current content. The negative conclusion rests on sustained Dutch-specific historical, literary, societal and structural-linguistic teaching, independent of proficiency and the remaining allocation uncertainty. See docs/qc/evidence/qualified-comparison-stage2-2026-11-15/cp-000309/external-review.json

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Dutch Studies degree is designed for non-native speakers of Dutch. It develops advanced Dutch language skills alongside the literature, history, art and society of the Netherlands, culminating in a supervised thesis normally written in Dutch.
audience.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for the documented Dutch Studies curriculum. UCR offers Dutch-language foundations, cultural comparison and substantial literary, artistic, film and language-research methods. Its strongest combinations do not sustain the programme’s continuing study of Dutch history, literature, society and structural and historical language. The 170 EC shown include distinct first-year philosophy and second-year digital-humanities courses. The disputed concentration credits and complete progression remain unverified.

curriculum.limitation: Supported subset: 170 of 180 EC. The current catalogue now distinguishes first-year Philosophy of Science from second-year Humanities in a Digital World. The third-year concentration allocation and complete entrant timetable/progression still need confirmation.

componentNotes.dst1-04: Part of the first-semester beginner language course. Students enrol in the zero-credit language class and its three credited writing/grammar, reading/vocabulary and speaking/listening examinations together; the class adds no extra credits.
componentNotes.dst1-05: Taken with the beginner writing/grammar and speaking/listening components, rather than as a standalone examination.
componentNotes.dst1-06: Taken with the beginner writing/grammar and reading/vocabulary components, rather than as a standalone examination.
componentNotes.dst1-09: Writing begins from approximately A2 Dutch. Reading/Vocabulary 1B is taken in parallel unless the required level is already demonstrated.
componentNotes.dst1-10: Entry requires at least A2 reading proficiency in Dutch.
componentNotes.dst1-11: Speaking and listening begin from approximately A2 Dutch. Reading/Vocabulary 1B is taken in parallel unless the required level is already demonstrated.
componentNotes.dst1-08: Designed for non-native speakers with basic Dutch at approximately A2/B1. Successful completion also forms part of the programme’s first-year study-advice requirements.
componentNotes.dst2-01: The programme’s ordered progression requires a pass in Writing/Grammar 1B before this introduction to second-language acquisition.
componentNotes.dst2-02: Entry requires a pass in first-year Speaking/Listening 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-05: Entry requires a pass in first-year Writing/Grammar 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-06: Entry requires passes in first-year Writing/Grammar 1B and Reading/Vocabulary 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-07: Entry requires a pass in first-year Reading/Vocabulary 1B.
componentNotes.dst2-10: Entry requires a pass in Writing about Culture, Language Acquisition II.
componentNotes.dst3-5813valsy: Taken after all Language Acquisition II components. The 10 EC comprises 5 EC for independent reading and an oral examination, and 5 EC for processing academic literature in spoken and written Dutch. It prepares students for the thesis.
componentNotes.dst3-5813vscr3y: Entry requires completion of all first- and second-year components and Academic Reading and Writing, Language Acquisition III. Students conduct independent research with supervision, normally writing in Dutch on a language or culture topic. The compulsory thesis seminar has the same entry requirements and carries 0 EC. Participation, including presenting the research at the programme’s student symposium, is required for the thesis credits. The complete cohort timetable remains under review.
componentNotes.dst3-elective-space-30: 30 EC of a minor, approved courses, study abroad or an approved internship within the elective space. Courses must have sufficient level and avoid overlap with the required curriculum; Honours College courses cannot count. Recognized 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus generally need no separate approval, subject to programme-specific overlap rules. An individual course package requires approval and normally allows at most 10 EC at level 100 and requires at least 10 EC at level 300 or above. Overlapping courses in the Second Language Acquisition or Digital Humanities and Artificial Intelligence minors require approved replacements.

comparisonScope.label: No close UCR comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 27 documented components totaling 170 EC: 120 distinct EC from the first two years, 10 EC academic reading and writing, a 10 EC thesis and 30 EC genuine approved open study. The compulsory zero-credit thesis seminar and known language/culture inquiry are considered.
comparisonScope.excluded: The disputed concentration allocation and exact coherent full 180-EC entrant timetable/progression. No unknown credits, future language exemption or concentration choice have been invented.

acceptance.targetContext: Leiden Dutch Studies BA, ordinary full-time September 2026 entry. No formal specialisation under the effective 2026 OER; Language/Culture are informal directions. All 170 documented EC retained; zero-credit seminar remains mandatory, not added credits.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified same-AI source-first final pass against underlying current official and UCR content and exact finished inputs; no independent human or separate-agent review.

uncertainties.fact: Third-year concentration parent 15 EC conflicts with 10 EC branches/two-module wording; exact coherent cohort timetable and dependent eligibility remain unverified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Either 10 or 15 EC of language, literary, art/historical or other permitted concentration study applies, with corrected placement/progression.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Give both informal directions their strongest substantive positive challenge. Neither plausible correction erases the known national cultural-linguistic core or supplies untaught continuing UCR Dutch inquiry. Exact total and progression remain excluded; no arithmetic reconciliation or automatic waiver is assumed.

adverseResolutions.resolution: A more permissive formal language/thesis rule or English/translated-source route applies.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: The negative proof already allows source translation and disregards missing proficiency as a sufficient veto. It rests on taught national cultural/linguistic substance; hypothetical Dutch-focused research is not treated as an actual UCR course sequence.
